sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: At the end of the calendar year and into the new year, the 99PI staff collects a bunch of short, joyful little stories that are fun to produce and make us happy.
sentences.zh: 在公历年末和新年伊始之际，99PI的全体员工收集了一堆短小、欢乐且制作起来很有趣的小故事，这些故事能给我们带来快乐。

sentences.en: We call them mini-stories.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为迷你故事。

sentences.en: This is the third and final episode of this batch and the 14th volume overall, and it's a good one.
sentences.zh: 这是这一系列的第三期也是最后一集，总计第14期，而且非常精彩。

sentences.en: We have stories about surprisingly architectural sports commentary, Ben Franklin's role in daylight saving time, and the origin of the fireball.
sentences.zh: 我们有一些关于出人意料的建筑学风格体育解说、本杰明·富兰克林在夏令时中的角色以及火球起源的故事。

sentences.en: Wake the kids.
sentences.zh: 叫醒孩子们。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请收看我们的节目。

sentences.en: So I'm with producer Emmett Fitzgerald, and Emmett, if past is precedent, you either have a sports story for us or an environmental story for us.
sentences.zh: 我和制作人埃米特·菲茨杰拉德在一起，埃米特，如果以过去为例，你要么为我们准备了一个体育故事，要么是一个环保故事。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: So which is it?
sentences.zh: 那么到底是哪个？

sentences.en: This week it's sports, Roman.
sentences.zh: 这周是体育，罗曼。

sentences.en: Fantastic.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I am ready.
sentences.zh: 我准备好了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 行吧。

sentences.en: So as I imagine you might have noticed, I got pretty into biking during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我想你可能注意到了，我在疫情期间迷上了骑行。

sentences.en: I did notice.
sentences.zh: 我确实注意到了。

sentences.en: You would put a little note on Slack that would say, like, I'm going to be gone for the next hour.
sentences.zh: 你会发一个小便签到Slack上，上面写着，比如，我接下来的一个小时不在。

sentences.en: And it was because you were biking.
sentences.zh: 原因就是你在骑车。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I had ridden bikes before COVID hit, but I kind of leveled up during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，在新冠疫情爆发之前我也骑过自行车，但在疫情期间我的水平可以说是升级了。

sentences.en: I took that canceled gym membership money and bought a road bike and some of the proper outfits and started riding up and down the East Bay Hills, torturing myself.
sentences.zh: 我把取消健身房会员省下来的钱买了一辆公路自行车和一些合适的装备，开始在东湾山骑上骑下，折磨自己。

sentences.en: And then a few months in, you know, to this new hobby, the Tour de France happened.
sentences.zh: 然后过了几个月，你知道的，就在我有了这个新爱好之后，环法自行车赛开始了。

sentences.en: And I had never really watched the Tour de France before, but I figured, you know, I'm into this now.
sentences.zh: 我以前其实从来没看过环法自行车赛，但我想，你知道的，我现在迷上这个了。

sentences.en: I'll give this a try.
sentences.zh: 我来试试看。

sentences.en: And what was immediately clear was that it's just like a very different spectacle from the other kinds of sports that I was used to watching.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的是，这与我习惯观看的其他体育赛事有着非常不同的观赏体验。

sentences.en: You know, things like basketball or soccer.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如篮球或足球。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then the biggest difference is really just one of time.
sentences.zh: 最大的不同其实就在于时间。

sentences.en: Like the Tour stretches on for several weeks and there's a stage nearly every day that lasts like four to six hours.
sentences.zh: 比如环法比赛持续好几个星期，几乎每天都有一个赛段，持续大约四到六个小时。

sentences.en: And within each stage, you know, there are moments of really intense, exciting action.
sentences.zh: 在每个赛段内，你知道的，都有非常激烈、令人兴奋的精彩瞬间。

sentences.en: But there's also long stretches where there isn't a whole lot happening, at least at least to my eyes as like an unsophisticated newbie.
sentences.zh: 但也有很长一段时间没有什么重大进展，至少在我这个孤陋寡闻的新手看来是这样的。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I wasn't giving it my undivided attention all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我并没有把全部注意力都放在上面。

sentences.en: It kind of became this sort of pleasant morning ritual that I would have on in the background as I, you know, drank my coffee and wrote my morning emails.
sentences.zh: 它在某种程度上变成了一种令人愉快的早晨仪式，当我喝着咖啡、写着早晨的电子邮件时，它就在背景里播放着。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It sounds kind of like slow TV, like watching a train over the course of 12 hours.
sentences.zh: 听起来有点像慢电视，就像花12个小时看一列火车开过。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全是这样。

sentences.en: That was at least at least that was how I was treating it.
sentences.zh: 至少，至少我是这么对待它的。

sentences.en: Maybe that's disrespectful to serious cycling fans.
sentences.zh: 也许这对严肃的骑行迷来说是一种不尊重。

sentences.en: But, you know, as I was doing this, I started to notice something kind of strange, which was that the cycling announcers, they don't just talk about cycling.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，当我这么做的时候，我开始注意到一件有点奇怪的事，那就是骑行解说员们不只是谈论骑行。

sentences.en: And one of the things that they really talk about a lot is architecture.
sentences.zh: 他们经常谈论的事情之一就是建筑。

sentences.en: Looking down here at the Church of Saint-Jean, built in 1862 in the shape of a Greek cross on the debris of the old parish church of Saint-Andeol.
sentences.zh: 向下看这里是圣让教堂，建于1862年，呈希腊十字形，建在圣安德奥尔旧教区教堂的废墟上。

sentences.en: Oh, it's got a porch-type bell tower with a roof flank with four pinnacles surmounted by a spire burning a huge cockle.
sentences.zh: 哦，它有一个门廊式钟楼，屋顶两侧有四个尖顶，上面有一个尖塔，燃烧着一头巨大的雄鸡。

sentences.en: Can't see it from this angle, though.
sentences.zh: 不过从这个角度看不到。

sentences.en: Oh, yes, I can.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，我能看到。

sentences.en: There, it is right on the front.
sentences.zh: 在那里，它就在正面。

sentences.en: Well spotted.
sentences.zh: 眼光不错。

sentences.en: Cock-a-doodle-loo.
sentences.zh: 喔喔啼。

sentences.en: Whoa, I could get into this.
sentences.zh: 哇，我能迷上这个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's like this extremely detailed architectural description of, you know, a church or something.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像是对教堂或其他东西的这种极其详细的建筑描述。

sentences.en: And if you watch a lot of this, you notice this all the time.
sentences.zh: 如果你看多了这个，你就会经常注意到这一点。

sentences.en: Like, the announcers will be talking about, you know,
sentences.zh: 比如，解说员会讨论，你知道的，

sentences.en: Team Jumbo-Visma's tactics and whether Primoz Roglic has what it takes to recover from that crash he suffered earlier in the stage.
sentences.zh: 珍宝维斯玛车队的战术，以及普里莫什·罗格利奇是否有能力从他在赛段早些时候遭遇的那次撞车事故中恢复过来。

sentences.en: And then suddenly, they're talking about, like, an abbey.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间，他们就在谈论，比如，一座修道院。

sentences.en: This is an abbey by the books of it, the old Abbey de L'Oucteux.
sentences.zh: 根据记录，这是一座修道院，旧的卢克修道院。

sentences.en: And it was at this abbey in 1940 that the Mona Lisa was moved to, along with more than a thousand other paintings from the Louvre,
sentences.zh: 1940年，蒙娜丽莎以及来自卢浮宫的一千多幅其他画作就被转移到了这座修道院，

sentences.en: to be put in storage for safety at the outbreak of the wall.
sentences.zh: 在战争爆发时为了安全而被存放在仓库里。

sentences.en: So it played a significant role in protecting some of the great artwork of not just of France, but of the world.
sentences.zh: 因此，它在保护不仅是法国、而且是世界的伟大艺术品方面发挥了重要作用。

sentences.en: Well, I'm really into this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我真的很喜欢这个。

sentences.en: This is like, I had no idea that the announcements had so much history and context.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，我完全不知道解说里有这么多的历史和背景。

sentences.en: That is, that is really stunning.
sentences.zh: 这真是，真是太惊艳了。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, I love it too.
sentences.zh: 对，对，我也很喜欢。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's just, I just find it so, it's so charming because it's like, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我只是觉得它太，它太迷人了，因为就像是，你知道的，

sentences.en: these serious sports announcers have like a sort of nearly encyclopedic knowledge of random buildings and little towns, like throughout the French countryside.
sentences.zh: 这些严肃的体育解说员对法国乡村各处随机的建筑物和小城镇有着近乎百科全书般的知识。

sentences.en: This is the valley where in 218 BC, Hannibal came through here with 90,000 men and 10,000 horsemen and 37 elephants on his way back home.
sentences.zh: 这就是公元前218年汉尼拔在回家的路上带着9万名士兵、1万名骑兵和37头大象经过的山谷。

sentences.en: And imagine what the road conditions were like in those days, Paul.
sentences.zh: 保罗，想象一下那时的路况是什么样的。

sentences.en: It was pretty tough for the elephants, I have to say, once they got over the top, because fortunately, with their large pads, they didn't slip too much on the snow.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，对大象来说相当艰难，一旦它们翻过山顶，因为幸运的是，凭借它们的大脚垫，它们在雪地上滑得不是太多。

sentences.en: Would there be Indian elephants?
sentences.zh: 会有印度象吗？

sentences.en: No, actually, there were African elephants.
sentences.zh: 不，实际上，那是非洲象。

sentences.en: Very unusual.
sentences.zh: 非常罕见。

sentences.en: I'm surprised they could train them.
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶他们能训练它们。

sentences.en: Four minutes and 18 seconds, 92 kilometers to go now.
sentences.zh: 还剩4分18秒，92公里。

sentences.en: And here's our poor man left on the way.
sentences.zh: 这是我们可怜的人留在路上。

sentences.en: I don't even know how to react to that.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道该如何对此作出反应。

sentences.en: That's just like, that's just stunning digression.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，这简直是惊人的题外话。

sentences.en: This is totally new to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说完全是新奇的。

sentences.en: Is this the way it's always been?
sentences.zh: 一直以来都是这样的吗？

sentences.en: Have they always been this like Wikipedia of architecture and world history at their fingertips and presented it when they're announcing the race?
sentences.zh: 他们是不是一直都是这样，把建筑和世界历史的维基百科烂熟于心，并在他们解说比赛时展示出来？

sentences.en: Yeah, I wanted to answer that question.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想回答这个问题。

sentences.en: And there's really one person who I think is best equipped to explain how we got here.
sentences.zh: 真的有一个人我认为最适合解释我们是如何走到这一步的。

sentences.en: And he's actually one of the announcers who you just heard there talking about African elephants.
sentences.zh: 他其实就是你刚才听到谈论非洲象的解说员之一。

sentences.en: His name is Phil Liggett.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫菲尔·利盖特。

sentences.en: And, you know, he's kind of like the most famous voice in professional cycling.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他可以说是职业自行车赛中最著名的声音。

sentences.en: In fact, there's a documentary about him that came out last year called Phil Liggett, The Voice of Cycling.
sentences.zh: 事实上，去年有一部关于他的纪录片上映了，叫做《菲尔·利盖特：自行车运动之音》。

sentences.en: And I talked to Phil on Zoom and he basically told me that he's been doing the Tour de France for decades.
sentences.zh: 我在Zoom上采访了菲尔，他基本上告诉我他解说环法自行车赛已经几十年了。

sentences.en: And in the very beginning, he was really one of the only English speaking cycling commentators in the world.
sentences.zh: 在最开始的时候，他真的是世界上仅有的几个英语自行车评论员之一。

sentences.en: Phil said, you know, it's a little hard to pinpoint exactly when the whole Chateau Church Abbey commentary got started.
sentences.zh: 菲尔说，你知道的，很难准确指出整个城堡、教堂、修道院的解说是什么时候开始的。

sentences.en: But he does remember one moment in particular.
sentences.zh: 但他确实特别记得一个时刻。

sentences.en: He was working with his long-term partner.
sentences.zh: 他当时和他的长期搭档一起工作。

sentences.en: They were a famous duo, the late, great Paul Sherwin.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个著名的二人组，已故伟大的保罗·舍温。

sentences.en: And the cameras panned over this dilapidated old abbey.
sentences.zh: 摄像机扫过这座破旧的老修道院。

sentences.en: And Phil looked at Paul just like, how did you know that?
sentences.zh: 菲尔看着保罗，简直就像是，你怎么知道的？

sentences.en: Like, how did you know that Louis XIV lived there?
sentences.zh: 就像是，你怎么知道路易十四住在那里？

sentences.en: Like, you're a cycling journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 就像是，你是个自行车记者。

sentences.en: And so how did he know it?
sentences.zh: 那他是怎么知道的呢？

sentences.en: Well, Paul had lived in France before when he was a pro cycliSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，保罗以前当过职业自行车手，在法国住过。

sentences.en: And I think that in that specific instance, it was just kind of like a fun fact that he had learned along the way.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在那个特定的情况下，这只是他在一路走来学到的一个有趣的事实。

sentences.en: But they started to do more of that, just like offering these like little bits of commentary about the landscape that the bikers were passing through,
sentences.zh: 但他们开始做更多这样的事情，就像提供这些关于自行车手经过的风景的小解说，

sentences.en: the buildings and the flora and the fauna.
sentences.zh: 建筑物、植物和动物。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think part of it at the time was that they were really trying to sell cycling to an American audience who was not as familiar with the sport as people in Europe.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我认为当时的部分原因在于他们真的在努力向美国观众推销自行车运动，美国观众对这项运动不像欧洲人那样熟悉。

sentences.en: But really, people from all over the world started writing in to say that they loved it.
sentences.zh: 但真的，世界各地的人们开始写信说他们喜欢这个。

sentences.en: And pretty soon, the Tour de France itself sort of realized what was happening.
sentences.zh: 很快，环法自行车赛本身就意识到了发生了什么。

sentences.en: The Tour de France brought on when they heard what we were doing and they started to sell their country more.
sentences.zh: 当环法听到我们在做什么时，他们加入了进来，并开始更多地推销他们的国家。

sentences.en: The Tour basically realized that they could use this to their advantage, what Phil and Paul were doing.
sentences.zh: 环法基本上意识到他们可以利用这一点为自己谋利，也就是菲尔和保罗在做的事情。

sentences.en: And Phil told me that this was all happening at a time when the race wasn't doing very well financially.
sentences.zh: 菲尔告诉我，这一切发生在一个比赛财政状况不太好的时期。

sentences.en: And people in France were actually getting kind of annoyed because it would lead to all of these road closures.
sentences.zh: 法国的人们实际上开始感到有点恼火，因为这会导致所有这些道路封闭。

sentences.en: There was a sense that it was like bad for business.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种感觉，这就像对生意不利。

sentences.en: And so when the Tour organizers picked up on what Phil and Paul were doing, they were like, oh, we could make this work for us.
sentences.zh: 所以当环法组织者注意到菲尔和保罗在做什么时，他们想，哦，我们可以让这为我们所用。

sentences.en: And almost reframe the Tour as like a three-week-long advertisement for the country of France.
sentences.zh: 几乎将环法重新构想为长达三周的法国国家广告。

sentences.en: So it's competitive cycling like wrapped in this advertisement for the French Tourism Board.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是包裹在法国旅游局广告中的竞技自行车运动。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: And so they started telling the camera operators to try and get pretty shots of the beautiful old churches and the bridges and waterfalls.
sentences.zh: 所以他们开始告诉摄像师去拍摄那些美丽的老教堂、桥梁和瀑布的漂亮镜头。

sentences.en: And they encouraged Phil and Paul to talk about that stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们鼓励菲尔和保罗谈论这些东西。

sentences.en: And for a while, they had to do all the research themselves.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，他们不得不自己做所有的研究。

sentences.en: But eventually, the Tour actually started producing this incredible book for them.
sentences.zh: 但最终，环法实际上开始为他们制作这本不可思议的书。

sentences.en: Which they call the Speaker's Guide to the Tour de France.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为《环法自行车赛解说指南》。

sentences.en: Tourist and historical information.
sentences.zh: 旅游和历史信息。

sentences.en: And in the book, every stage and every monument or old house or garden or bird in that region that we passed through is pictured in here.
sentences.zh: 在这本书里，我们经过的那个地区的每一个赛段、每一个纪念碑、老房子、花园或鸟类都图文并茂地记录在这里。

sentences.en: So it's basically a guidebook to the French countryside, except it's designed exclusively for Phil and like a handful of other people who are cycling commentators for the tour.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上是一本法国乡村的指南，除了它是专门为菲尔和少数其他为巡回赛做自行车评论的人设计的。

sentences.en: Like exclusively for them, like meaning that they printed it just for them.
sentences.zh: 就像专门为他们一样，意思是他们是专门为他们印制的。

sentences.en: Like it's not available to the general public at all.
sentences.zh: 就像根本不对公众开放一样。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: No, like you can't even – it's like pretty hard to find a copy even if you're like searching on like eBay and stuff.
sentences.zh: 不，就像你甚至——即使你在eBay之类的网站上搜索，也很难找到一本。

sentences.en: Like they don't even – even if you're like a cycling journalist, you can't get a copy.
sentences.zh: 就像他们甚至——即使你是一名自行车记者，你也拿不到一本。

sentences.en: It's just like people – it's like for the handful of people who are on the mic doing the commentating for the various TV stations that are broadcasting the event.
sentences.zh: 这就像是人们——这是为了在转播赛事的各个电视台担任解说的少数几个人准备的。

sentences.en: And Phil showed me his just like through the Zoom and, you know, it's basically just like this giant homemade book with like hundreds of hundreds of pages.
sentences.zh: 菲尔通过Zoom向我展示了他的书，你知道的，它基本上就像一本巨大的自制书，有几百页。

sentences.en: And he said that it's really all put together by this one person.
sentences.zh: 他说这真的是由这一个人拼凑起来的。

sentences.en: And every year when the tour route is announced the following year in October, it's her job to drive every inch of the route,
sentences.zh: 每年10月公布第二年的巡回赛路线时，她的工作就是开车巡视路线的每一英寸，

sentences.en: all two and a half to three and a half thousand miles of it.
sentences.zh: 所有的两千五百到三千五百英里。

sentences.en: And basically document all of the points of interest that the cameras might linger on during the race.
sentences.zh: 并基本上记录下比赛期间摄像机可能会驻留的所有兴趣点。

sentences.en: Every chateau, every palace, every garden, the mountains, the flora and the fauna, I put it all in this book.
sentences.zh: 每一座城堡、每一座宫殿、每一个花园、山脉、植物和动物，我都把它们放进了这本书里。

sentences.en: And then on the day before the tour starts, the organization gives every commentator a copy of the book in English and French.
sentences.zh: 然后在比赛开始前一天，组织会给每个解说员一本英文和法文的副本。

sentences.en: And each entry just has like a bunch of interesting tidbits and facts about particular buildings or bridges that, you know, the cameras might pass over.
sentences.zh: 每个条目都有一堆关于特定建筑物或桥梁的有趣花絮和事实，摄像机可能会掠过这些地方。

sentences.en: But there's this moment in the broadcast that Phil described to me where it's like you have to make sure that you have found the right thing.
sentences.zh: 但在菲尔向我描述的广播中，有一个时刻，你必须确保你找到了正确的东西。

sentences.en: Like what you're looking at on the cameras is the thing that you're – you don't want to read the facts for the wrong chateau.
sentences.zh: 就像你在摄像机上看到的东西就是你正在——你不想为一个错误的城堡读出这些事实。

sentences.en: And so he described all these moments to me where he would just be looking over and seeing his partner, Paul, like frantically trying to find the right building in the book.
sentences.zh: 因此，他向我描述了所有这些时刻，他会环顾四周，看到他的搭档保罗在书疯狂地试图找到正确的建筑。

sentences.en: And I'm watching Paul savagely rip the book apart to find a picture of this darn chateau.
sentences.zh: 而我看着保罗疯狂地把书撕开，为了找到这座该死的城堡的照片。

sentences.en: And I'm just dying to laugh.
sentences.zh: 我简直快笑死了。

sentences.en: I've told him I can't because I'm live on air.
sentences.zh: 我告诉过他我不能笑，因为我在直播。

sentences.en: And I can see the sweat on his brow because he's desperate.
sentences.zh: 我能看到他额头上的汗水，因为他很绝望。

sentences.en: But then all of a sudden, he'll come in.
sentences.zh: 但突然之间，他就会插话进来。

sentences.en: I'll say, what do you think of that, Paul?
sentences.zh: 我会说，保罗，你觉得那个怎么样？

sentences.en: And then Paul, you know, who had in the meantime had, you know, been – had found the right page,
sentences.zh: 然后保罗，你知道的，与此同时已经——已经找到了正确的那一页，

sentences.en: would just coolly read off a few interesting facts about the building as if he knew them, you know, right off the top of his head.
sentences.zh: 就会冷冷静静地读出关于这座建筑的一些有趣的事实，就好像他知道这些一样，你知道的，脱口而出。

sentences.en: What do we know about that, Paul?
sentences.zh: 关于这个我们知道些什么，保罗？

sentences.en: Well, the Pontegoo, this is one of those medieval villages I was telling you about a little earlier.
sentences.zh: 嗯，蓬特古，这就是我刚才跟你提到过的那些中世纪村庄之一。

sentences.en: They were all very much fortified.
sentences.zh: 它们都经过了大量的防御加固。

sentences.en: They've got a lot of very narrow streets in there.
sentences.zh: 那里有很多非常狭窄的街道。

sentences.en: It's situated right on the Uves Valley, and it was extremely important in years gone by for its military and military control.
sentences.zh: 它位于于韦河谷上，在过去的年代里，对于军事和军事控制来说极其重要。

sentences.en: Just look and there's a problem there at the back with a flat tire.
sentences.zh: 你看，后面有个轮胎瘪了的问题。

sentences.en: Yes, he's waiting for a tire.
sentences.zh: 对，他在等换轮胎。

sentences.en: You'd never know.
sentences.zh: 你根本猜不到。

sentences.en: He'd been, you know, tearing through this book trying to come up with that, you know, fact about the military might of the Uves Valley or whatever, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他一直在猛翻这本书，想找出关于于韦河谷军事实力之类的那些事实。

sentences.en: No, I mean, they're amazing broadcasters.
sentences.zh: 不，我的意思是，他们是了不起的广播员。

sentences.en: That's what you really take away from these clips is just how good they are at their job.
sentences.zh: 你从这些片段中真正体会到的是，他们对自己的工作是多么擅长。

sentences.en: Yeah, they're – yeah, they're really talented.
sentences.zh: 对，他们——对，他们真的很有才华。

sentences.en: And Phil, you know, he says he gets emails all the time from people who appreciate this detail and want to know, you know, like, the exact route from the tour from that past year
sentences.zh: 而且菲尔，你知道的，他说他经常收到邮件，来自那些欣赏这种细节并想知道诸如过去那一年环赛确切路线的人

sentences.en: because they saw this, like, particular village that they thought was beautiful.
sentences.zh: 因为他们看到了这个他们觉得很美的特定村庄。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think – and in France, too, it also has worked.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为——而且在法国也是如此，这也行得通。

sentences.en: Like, the tour is thought to be a real showcase for the country now.
sentences.zh: 比如，环赛现在被认为是这个国家真正的展示窗口。

sentences.en: And towns will actually pay money to have the tour go through their town because it will bring in, you know, the tourist revenue
sentences.zh: 城镇甚至会付钱让环赛穿过他们的城镇，因为它会带来，你知道的，旅游收入

sentences.en: and also that, you know, people from all around the world will kind of get a chance to see their town
sentences.zh: 还有，你知道的，来自世界各地的人们将有机会看到他们的城镇

sentences.en: and maybe hear someone like Phil describe, you know, their chateau.
sentences.zh: 也许还能听到像菲尔这样的人描述，你知道的，他们的城堡。

sentences.en: Their 14th century abbey.
sentences.zh: 他们14世纪的修道院。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: And they might want to come visit sometime.
sentences.zh: 而且他们可能什么时候想来参观一下。

sentences.en: Well, that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 哇，这太厉害了。

sentences.en: I am really, really impressed by Phil as a broadcaster, and it's so much fun to listen to him.
sentences.zh: 我真的、真的很佩服作为广播员的菲尔，听他说话太有意思了。

sentences.en: So, this is so great.
sentences.zh: 所以，这太棒了。

sentences.en: I'm now – I'm into it.
sentences.zh: 我现在——我迷上了。

sentences.en: I'm now going to watch the Tour de France.
sentences.zh: 我接下来要去看环法自行车赛了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Like, I love this idea.
sentences.zh: 比如，我很喜欢这个主意。

sentences.en: Yeah, put it on in the background at the very leaSt.
sentences.zh: 对，至少把它在背景里放着。

sentences.en: That sounds great.
sentences.zh: 听起来真不错。

sentences.en: Emmett, thank you so much for introducing me to Phil Liggett.
sentences.zh: 埃米特，非常感谢你把我介绍给菲尔·利格特。

sentences.en: I think that that's a gem of a human.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他真是一个宝藏般的人。

sentences.en: Thank you, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，罗曼。

sentences.en: Okay, so I'm here with Chris Perube.
sentences.zh: 好的，我现在和克里斯·佩鲁韦在一起。

sentences.en: Chris, what do you have for us?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，你给我们带来了什么？

sentences.en: Hi, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嗨，罗曼。

sentences.en: So, over the summer, you might remember, we did a story about daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 所以，夏天的时候你可能还记得，我们做过一篇关于夏令时的报道。

sentences.en: Yes, saving no S.
sentences.zh: 对，saving没有S。

sentences.en: Saving with no S, yes.
sentences.zh: saving没有S，对。

sentences.en: The biggest news you can use I have ever provided on this podcast is that it is daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 我在这档播客中提供过的最实用重磅新闻就是，现在是夏令时。

sentences.en: So, I have a follow-up to that story.
sentences.zh: 所以，我对那篇报道有一个后续。

sentences.en: And before I get there, just a quick recap of what we talked about with daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 在我讲到那之前，先快速回顾一下我们之前讨论的关于夏令时的事情。

sentences.en: It was episode 443.
sentences.zh: 那是第443期节目。

sentences.en: We told the story of William Willett.
sentences.zh: 我们讲述了威廉·维利特的故事。

sentences.en: He's kind of the father of daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 他可以说是夏令时的之父。

sentences.en: He was this British architect who campaigned for the idea for years.
sentences.zh: 他是一位英国建筑师，为这个想法奔走呼吁了好多年。

sentences.en: And then he died.
sentences.zh: 然后他去世了。

sentences.en: And one year after his death, the British Parliament finally tried out daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 在他去世一年后，英国议会终于试行了夏令时。

sentences.en: And that's why we have it today.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天拥有它的原因。

sentences.en: There's a commemorative sundial to him in Kent.
sentences.zh: 在肯特郡有一个为他建立的纪念日晷。

sentences.en: Beautiful, wrap-it-up-with-a-nice-bow type of story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很完美的、画上圆满句号的故事。

sentences.en: Yes, I remember that part of the story.
sentences.zh: 是的，我记得故事的那一部分。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: So, after I put out that story, I got quite a few emails from listeners who were saying, love the story, great job, but wait a second.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我发布了那个报道后，我收到了不少听众的邮件，他们说，故事很棒，干得漂亮，但等一下。

sentences.en: I thought Benjamin Franklin invented daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 我以为是本杰明·富兰克林发明了夏令时。

sentences.en: Benjamin Franklin, like, yeah, the American founding father, Benjamin Franklin.
sentences.zh: 本杰明·富兰克林，就像，是的，美国国父，本杰明·富兰克林。

sentences.en: Yeah, like Benjamin Franklin, Benjamin Franklin.
sentences.zh: 对，就像本杰明·富兰克林，本杰明·富兰克林。

sentences.en: Who's responsible for so many things, you know, according to lore.
sentences.zh: 根据传说，他应对了如此多的事情负责。

sentences.en: Well, and as soon as I started getting these emails, I was thinking, is he responsible for it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我一收到这些邮件就开始想，这真的是他负责的吗？

sentences.en: Like, he invented so much other stuff.
sentences.zh: 就像，他发明了那么多别的东西。

sentences.en: Like, it seems entirely plausible.
sentences.zh: 比如，这听起来完全有可能。

sentences.en: So, I decided I have to get to the bottom of this.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定必须查个水落石出。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, I did a little investigation.
sentences.zh: 于是我做了一番调查。

sentences.en: All right, let's hear it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，说来听听。

sentences.en: So, I called up this guy.
sentences.zh: 所以我给这个人打了电话。

sentences.en: Hello, is this Ranger Thomas Daniels?
sentences.zh: 喂，请问是托马斯·丹尼尔斯护林员吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是。

sentences.en: Should I call you Ranger Daniels?
sentences.zh: 我该叫你丹尼尔斯护林员吗？

sentences.en: What is the right way to refer to you?
sentences.zh: 称呼你的正确方式是什么？

sentences.en: You just call me Tom.
sentences.zh: 你直接叫我汤姆就行。

sentences.en: So, Park Ranger Tom Daniels works at the Independence National Park in Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 所以，公园护林员汤姆·丹尼尔斯在费城的独立国家公园工作。

sentences.en: It includes lots of American landmarks, including the Liberty Bell and also the Benjamin Franklin Museum.
sentences.zh: 那里包含许多美国地标，包括自由钟和本杰明·富兰克林博物馆。

sentences.en: And at the park, he is their resident Benjamin Franklin nut.
sentences.zh: 在公园里，他是那里的常驻本杰明·富兰克林狂热爱好者。

sentences.en: I would say he's always been a fascinating character for me.
sentences.zh: 我会说他对我来说一直是一个迷人的人物。

sentences.en: And the more you learn about him, the more you're amazed by how much he actually accomplished in one lifespan.
sentences.zh: 你对他的了解越多，就越对他在一生中取得的成就感到惊叹。

sentences.en: So, we talked for a while about Franklin.
sentences.zh: 所以我们聊了好一会儿关于富兰克林的事。

sentences.en: I explained the whole thing, you know, William Willett, the angry emails.
sentences.zh: 我把整件事都解释了一遍，你知道的，威廉·维利特，那些愤怒的邮件。

sentences.en: And I finally asked him the question, did Benjamin Franklin invent Daylight Saving Time?
sentences.zh: 我终于问了他那个问题，本杰明·富兰克林发明了夏令时吗？

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: what's fascinating about that is I think this is one of the stories where Benjamin Franklin becomes so famous that he starts getting things attributed to him that are not necessarily attributable to him.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，最迷人的是，我认为这是一个这样的故事：本杰明·富兰克林名气太大，以至于开始有一些并非他所做的事被归功于他。

sentences.en: And Daylight Saving Time is one of those.
sentences.zh: 夏令时就是其中之一。

sentences.en: And that's the end of the story.
sentences.zh: 故事到此结束。

sentences.en: Benjamin Franklin did not invent Daylight Saving Time.
sentences.zh: 本杰明·富兰克林并没有发明夏令时。

sentences.en: No, there's more.
sentences.zh: 不，还有呢。

sentences.en: I would expect a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 我本期待能多听一点。

sentences.en: There's a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 还有一点点。

sentences.en: I know this is a mini story, but it's not quite that brief.
sentences.zh: 我知道这是一个迷你故事，但也没有那么简短。

sentences.en: So, there is a funny connection between Benjamin Franklin and Daylight Saving Time.
sentences.zh: 所以，本杰明·富兰克林和夏令时之间确实有一个有趣的联系。

sentences.en: It comes from 1776 after the Declaration of Independence was signed and the Continental Congress was getting ready to go to war with Britain for the independence of the United States.
sentences.zh: 这要追溯到1776年，在《独立宣言》签署之后，大陆会议正准备为美国的独立与英国开战。

sentences.en: And they wanted French military support to fight the war.
sentences.zh: 他们想要法国提供军事支持来打这场仗。

sentences.en: So, they decided we need to send somebody over there who will win over French hearts and minds and who better to send than Benjamin Franklin, the world-famous inventor and writer.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定，我们需要派一个人去那里，赢得法国人民的心，还有谁比世界著名的发明家和作家本杰明·富兰克林更适合派遣呢？

sentences.en: So, they sent Benjamin Franklin over to France as a diplomat and –
sentences.zh: 所以他们派本杰明·富兰克林作为外交官去法国，然后——

sentences.en: His charge is to essentially try and secure a formal alliance with the French.
sentences.zh: 他的职责基本上是试图争取与法国结成正式同盟。

sentences.en: There's no guarantee that we were going to be capable of winning independence.
sentences.zh: 当时并不能保证我们一定有能力赢得独立。

sentences.en: So, this was going to take a lot of convincing.
sentences.zh: 所以这需要大量的说服工作。

sentences.en: So, Franklin really dived into it.
sentences.zh: 因此，富兰克林真的全身心投入其中。

sentences.en: He really ingratiated himself into French society.
sentences.zh: 他真正融入了法国社会。

sentences.en: So, what does that mean, to ingratiate himself into French society?
sentences.zh: 那么，融入法国社会是什么意思呢？

sentences.en: It basically means he was going to a lot of parties.
sentences.zh: 这基本上意味着他参加了很多派对。

sentences.en: So, every night, Ben Franklin was just staying up really late, hanging out with all these important French people.
sentences.zh: 所以每天晚上，本杰明·富兰克林都熬得很晚，和这些重要的法国人混在一起。

sentences.en: According to some accounts, he was basically living like a college student.
sentences.zh: 根据一些记载，他基本上过着像大学生一样的生活。

sentences.en: And then, one day, Benjamin Franklin's in Paris and there's a loud noise outside his window.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天，本杰明·富兰克林在巴黎，他的窗外传出了很大的声音。

sentences.en: And he wakes up and he looks outside and he sees that the sun is coming up.
sentences.zh: 他醒来向外看，发现太阳正在升起。

sentences.en: And it's 6 or 7 a.m.
sentences.zh: 当时是早上6点或7点。

sentences.en: And this is a revelation for Benjamin Franklin.
sentences.zh: 这对本杰明·富兰克林来说是一个全新的启示。

sentences.en: And he writes an essay in the Journal of Paris.
sentences.zh: 他在《巴黎杂志》上写了一篇短文。

sentences.en: And it's called an economical project.
sentences.zh: 这篇短文被称为《一个经济计划》。

sentences.en: And he basically gently chastises the citizens of Paris for not getting up with the sun.
sentences.zh: 他基本上温和地责备了巴黎市民没有跟随太阳一同起居。

sentences.en: The gall of that diplomat to go in there and tell them how to do things.
sentences.zh: 那个外交官真是好大的胆子，竟然跑去那里告诉别人该怎么做事。

sentences.en: Roman, here.
sentences.zh: 罗曼在这。

sentences.en: Actually, Tom read me an excerpt from an economical project.
sentences.zh: 事实上，汤姆给我读了《一个经济计划》中的一个摘录。

sentences.en: He says,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: And your readers, who with me, have never seen any sign of sunshine before noon, and seldom regard the astronomical part of the almanac,
sentences.zh: 而你们的读者，和我一样，在中午之前从未见过任何阳光的迹象，也很少关注年鉴中的天文部分，

sentences.en: will be as much astonished as I was when they hear of his rising so early, and especially when I assure them that he gives light as soon as he rises.
sentences.zh: 当他们听到太阳起得这么早时，一定会像我一样感到震惊，尤其是当我向他们保证太阳一升起就会带来光芒时。

sentences.en: That is Benjamin Franklin's great revelation, is that the sun comes up in the morning.
sentences.zh: 这就是本杰明·富兰克林的伟大发现，原来早晨太阳是会升起来的。

sentences.en: Well, you get a little bit from his tone here of, like, what he's trying to do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从他的语气中，你可以感受到一点他试图在做什么。

sentences.en: He's overdoing it a little bit in a fun way, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他以一种有趣的方式稍微有些用力过猛了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, Tom called this essay satirical.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，汤姆称这篇文章是讽刺性的。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是对的。

sentences.en: And it includes these recommendations at the end that are pretty outlandish.
sentences.zh: 最后它包含了一些相当离谱的建议。

sentences.en: One of the regulations says,
sentences.zh: 其中一条规定说，

sentences.en: Every morning, as soon as the sun rises, let all the bells in every church be set ringing.
sentences.zh: 每天早晨，太阳一升起，就让每一座教堂的所有钟声都敲响。

sentences.en: And if that is not sufficient, let cannon be fired in every street to wake the sluggards effectually and make them open their eyes to see their true intereSt.
sentences.zh: 如果这还不够，就在每条街上鸣放礼炮，以彻底唤醒懒虫们，让他们睁开眼睛看到自己的真正利益所在。

sentences.en: Well, firing a cannon seems pretty extreme, but I have to kind of, I kind of dig it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，鸣放礼炮似乎有点极端，但我有点——我挺喜欢的。

sentences.en: I mean, Roman, what else is going to awaken the sluggards, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，罗曼，还有什么能唤醒那些懒虫呢，对吧？

sentences.en: You have to effectually awaken those sluggards.
sentences.zh: 你必须有效地唤醒那些懒虫。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: So in conclusion, Benjamin Franklin did not invent daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 所以总结一下，本杰明·富兰克林并没有发明夏令时。

sentences.en: He did write this funny essay about everyone in Paris waking up to the sounds of cannons being fired, which I guess is why people make that mistake,
sentences.zh: 他确实写了这篇有趣的短文，关于每个人在鸣放礼炮的声音中醒来，我想这就是为什么人们会犯那个错误，

sentences.en: because it's also about waking up earlier with the sun.
sentences.zh: 因为它也讲了随着太阳升起而更早醒来的事。

sentences.en: But there's something bigger going on here, which is that lots of inventions get attributed to Benjamin Franklin that he is not responsible for.
sentences.zh: 但这里面有更深层的原因，那就是许多发明都被归功于本杰明·富兰克林，而这些并不是他做的。

sentences.en: And Tom told me this actually happens at his job sometimes.
sentences.zh: 汤姆告诉我，这在他的工作中确实有时会发生。

sentences.en: I think the most famous one is people think that he invented, they think he invented the light bulb, which of course was Thomas Edison.
sentences.zh: 我认为最著名的一个是人们以为他发明了，他们以为他发明了电灯泡，而这当然是托马斯·爱迪生的发明。

sentences.en: I think the confusion comes from Franklin's experiments with electricity.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种混淆来自于富兰克林对电的实验。

sentences.en: Some other common ones I found on the internet, there are people who believe Benjamin Franklin invented the streetlight.
sentences.zh: 我在网上发现的其他一些常见的误解是，有人相信本杰明·富兰克林发明了路灯。

sentences.en: He did not invent the streetlight.
sentences.zh: 他并没有发明路灯。

sentences.en: He was involved in improving a certain design of streetlight.
sentences.zh: 他参与改进了某种特定设计的路灯。

sentences.en: There is actually a page on the Franklin Institute website dedicated to quotes that are falsely attributed to Ben Franklin.
sentences.zh: 富兰克林研究所的网站上实际上有一个专门的页面，列出了被错误归功于本杰明·富兰克林的引言。

sentences.en: So would you like to hear an example?
sentences.zh: 所以你想听一个例子吗？

sentences.en: I would love to, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我很想听，对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Any fool can criticize, condemn, and complain.
sentences.zh: 任何傻瓜都可以批评、谴责和抱怨。

sentences.en: And most fools do.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数傻瓜也确实这么做。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 噢，好吧。

sentences.en: That sounds very Franklin-y.
sentences.zh: 听起来很像富兰克林会说的话。

sentences.en: Or, yeah, it's kind of Mark Twain-y as well.
sentences.zh: 或者，对，这也挺像马克·吐温风格的。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's a little more modern than that.
sentences.zh: 这比那个要更现代一点。

sentences.en: That was actually said by Dale Carnegie, the guy who wrote How to Win Friends and Influence People.
sentences.zh: 这其实是戴尔·卡耐基说的，就是写过《人性的弱点》的那个人。

sentences.en: So someone who's pretty different.
sentences.zh: 所以是一个相当不同的人。

sentences.en: He did not invent daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 他并没有发明夏令时。

sentences.en: He did not invent daylight saving time, not to diminish his other accomplishments.
sentences.zh: 他并没有发明夏令时，这并不是要贬低他的其他成就。

sentences.en: Please be careful when you're reading those articles online that say the 10 amazing things created by Ben Franklin.
sentences.zh: 你在网上阅读那些说本·富兰克林发明的10件惊人事情的文章时，请务必小心。

sentences.en: Please approach those with suspicion.
sentences.zh: 对这些文章请保持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: That's a good warning.
sentences.zh: 这个警告很好。

sentences.en: Thanks so much, Chris.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，克里斯。

sentences.en: Thanks, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，罗曼。

sentences.en: Coming up, we get to the bottom of the fire pole after this.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将在广告后一探消防滑杆的究竟。

sentences.en: So I'm here with producer Lasha McDon.
sentences.zh: 所以我和制片人拉莎·麦克唐在一起。

sentences.en: Hey, Lasha.
sentences.zh: 嘿，拉莎。

sentences.en: Hey, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼。

sentences.en: So what do you have for us?
sentences.zh: 你给我们带来了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I wanted to talk with you about fire poles.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想跟你聊聊消防滑杆。

sentences.en: Oh, excellent.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: I was just thinking about fire poles and then I didn't know what they were all about.
sentences.zh: 我刚好在想消防滑杆，但我不知道它们是怎么回事。

sentences.en: But you're talking about the shiny brass poles that firefighters lie down to get from the second floor to the first floor.
sentences.zh: 但你指的是那种亮晶晶的黄铜杆，消防员从二楼滑到一楼时会用它。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And sometimes from the third floor to the first floor.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至从三楼滑到一楼。

sentences.en: So the fire pole as an object is pretty symbolic of the firefighting profession, right?
sentences.zh: 所以消防滑杆作为一种物品，相当具有消防职业的象征意义，对吧？

sentences.en: But the actual use of the pole has kind of become a thing of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 但这种杆子的实际使用现在已经有点成为过去了。

sentences.en: If you learned about firefighters as a kid, maybe from your parents or teachers or even a storybook, you were probably told about the pole.
sentences.zh: 如果你小时候了解过消防员，也许是从父母、老师甚至故事书里，你可能听说过这种杆子。

sentences.en: Because at one time, it was in nearly every fire station.
sentences.zh: 因为在当时，几乎每个消防局都有它。

sentences.en: Any guesses why?
sentences.zh: 猜猜为什么？

sentences.en: Well, my first guess is the obvious one, which is it gets you from one floor to the other very, very faSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的第一个猜测是显而易见的那个，就是它能让你非常非常快地从一个楼层到达另一个楼层。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Fast was the way to go.
sentences.zh: 快就是王道。

sentences.en: Putting out a fire fast meant getting to the fire faSt.
sentences.zh: 快速灭火意味着以最快的速度到达火灾现场。

sentences.en: And for years, fire poles have helped firefighters do that.
sentences.zh: 多年来，消防滑杆一直帮助消防员做到这一点。

sentences.en: But the origin story of the pole is actually pretty interesting.
sentences.zh: 但这种杆子的起源故事其实相当有趣。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, lay it on me.
sentences.zh: 那就告诉我吧。

sentences.en: I called up retired Chicago Battalion Chief DeKalb Walcott, Jr.
sentences.zh: 我打电话采访了芝加哥退休消防营长小德卡尔夫·沃尔科特。

sentences.en: My name is DeKalb Walcott, Jr.
sentences.zh: 我的名字叫小德卡尔夫·沃尔科特。

sentences.en: I moved through the ranks from fireman, engineer, lieutenant, captain, and served four years as a battalion chief.
sentences.zh: 我的职级从消防员、工程师、中尉、上尉一路晋升，并担任了四年营长。

sentences.en: So Chief Walcott is fine.
sentences.zh: 所以叫他沃尔科特营长就行了。

sentences.en: Chief Walcott is now a firefighter historian.
sentences.zh: 沃尔科特营长现在是一位消防员历史学家。

sentences.en: He's been archiving Black firefighter history in Chicago, where our fire pole origin story takes place.
sentences.zh: 他一直在整理芝加哥的黑人消防员历史，我们的消防滑杆起源故事就发生在那里。

sentences.en: But Roman, before we get to the poles, let's talk about the firefighters.
sentences.zh: 但罗曼，在我们讲到滑杆之前，先来聊聊消防员吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The first firefighters were the Bucket Brigade.
sentences.zh: 最早的消防员是水桶方阵。

sentences.en: This was the 1600s, before engines and hoses.
sentences.zh: 那是16世纪，在消防车和水带出现之前。

sentences.en: They would have a long line of men, women, children, slaves, freedmen, whoever could hold a bucket, probably.
sentences.zh: 他们会排成长队，由男人、女人、儿童、奴隶、获得自由的人组成，大概只要是能拿得动水桶的人都行。

sentences.en: And they passed the buckets on until they got to the seat of the fire or the person that was first in line that was dumped in the water.
sentences.zh: 他们一桶接一桶地传递，直到送到火源处，或者由排在最前面的人把水泼进去。

sentences.en: The Bucket Brigade was basically a long human chain.
sentences.zh: 水桶方阵基本上就是一条长长的人肉链条。

sentences.en: Over time, they improved the system of firefighting with the goal of putting fires out as fast as possible.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，他们改进了灭火系统，目标是以尽可能快的速度扑灭火灾。

sentences.en: By the 1800s, there were engines being pulled by horses.
sentences.zh: 到了19世纪，出现了由马匹拉动的消防车。

sentences.en: But one thing didn't change throughout this whole time period.
sentences.zh: 但在这整个时期内，有一件事没有变。

sentences.en: Each group of firefighters, which were called fire companies, were in furious competition to fight the same fire.
sentences.zh: 每一组消防员（被称为消防连）都在激烈竞争，争相去扑灭同一场火灾。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: So why were they competing?
sentences.zh: 那他们为什么要竞争呢？

sentences.en: Originally, volunteer companies were basically at the whim of the insurance carrier.
sentences.zh: 最初，志愿消防连基本上全听保险公司的差遣。

sentences.en: Whoever got to the fire first, put water on the fire first, were the ones who were paid.
sentences.zh: 谁先到达火灾现场，谁先把水泼到火上，就能拿到报酬。

sentences.en: And no one else was paid, even if they got there a little bit later?
sentences.zh: 其他人哪怕晚到了一会儿也拿不到钱吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Essentially, insurance companies would pay only one fire company.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，保险公司只支付给一个消防连报酬。

sentences.en: The one that made it to the scene, hooked up to the hydrant, and put out the fire firSt.
sentences.zh: 也就是那个赶到现场、接上消火栓并第一个把火扑灭的消防连。

sentences.en: And with so much competition, things got messy.
sentences.zh: 在如此激烈的竞争下，情况变得一团糟。

sentences.en: This seems like a really bad system.
sentences.zh: 这听起来真是个糟糕的系统。

sentences.en: It's a bad setup.
sentences.zh: 这是一种糟糕的设置。

sentences.en: So tell me more about how it got more messy.
sentences.zh: 所以跟我多讲讲它是怎么变得更乱的吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I mean, well, so first of all, most firefighters weren't getting paid much at all.
sentences.zh: 我是说，首先，大多数消防员根本拿不到多少薪水。

sentences.en: Insurance companies would offer incentives to particular fire stations over others.
sentences.zh: 保险公司会向某些特定的消防站提供奖励，而不是所有消防站。

sentences.en: And so those fire stations sometimes did what they could to slow down their rivals.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些消防站有时会想方设法拖慢竞争对手的速度。

sentences.en: DeKalb told me there was also a huge culture of drinking among volunteer firefighters.
sentences.zh: 德卡尔夫告诉我，志愿消防员中间还存在着严重的酗酒文化。

sentences.en: Many firehouses were even outfitted with their own bars.
sentences.zh: 许多消防局甚至配备了他们自己的酒吧。

sentences.en: And in Chicago, DeKalb said that taverns would sometimes give alcohol out to firefighters at the scene of a fire to help them get their bravery up.
sentences.zh: 德卡尔夫说，在芝加哥，小酒馆有时会在火灾现场给消防员提供酒精饮品，来帮助他们鼓起勇气。

sentences.en: And sometimes that alcohol helped facilitate full-on brawls on the street.
sentences.zh: 有时这些酒精还会促成街头的大规模斗殴。

sentences.en: And they would get into fights, not only with the public, but also with the other fire companies they were competing againSt.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅与公众发生冲突，还与他们正在竞争的其他消防连大打出手。

sentences.en: There were a lot of complaints by the public also, because here you have a fire company fighting in the street when they should be putting water on fire.
sentences.zh: 公众也有很多抱怨，因为本该在街上灭火的消防连却在街上打架。

sentences.en: So there'd be, like, fire consuming a building, and firefighters from different stations would be having, like, a brawl in the street right in front of it.
sentences.zh: 所以可能会出现这样的情况：一栋建筑正在被大火吞噬，而不同消防站的消防员就在它正前方的街道上群殴。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's a terrifying image.
sentences.zh: 这画面太吓人了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And it's in this competitive atmosphere that a new fire station, Engine Company 21, is formed.
sentences.zh: 正是在这种竞争氛围中，一个新的消防站——第21消防连成立了。

sentences.en: Engine 21 was an all-Black fire company.
sentences.zh: 第21消防连是一个全由黑人组成的消防连。

sentences.en: And actually, Engine 21 was the first paid Black fire company in the country.
sentences.zh: 事实上，第21消防连是全国第一支有薪水的黑人消防连。

sentences.en: They had approximately eight Black members.
sentences.zh: 他们大约有八名黑人成员。

sentences.en: Many of those members were ex-Civil War veterans and also slaves.
sentences.zh: 许多成员都是退伍的南北战争老兵以及奴隶。

sentences.en: So it was 1872, and for the very first time, the mayor of Chicago, Joseph Medill, allowed Black people to join the Chicago Fire Department.
sentences.zh: 当时是1872年，芝加哥市长约瑟夫·梅迪尔破天荒地允许黑人加入芝加哥消防局。

sentences.en: As you can imagine, members of the newly formed Engine 21 firehouse felt a particular need to prove themselves.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，新成立的第21消防连的成员们感到有一种特殊的需要去证明自己。

sentences.en: And Engine 21 is credited with coming up with the fire pole.
sentences.zh: 而第21消防连被认为是消防滑杆的发明者。

sentences.en: Oh, this is so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 哦，这太迷人了。

sentences.en: Okay, so how did that happen?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那是怎么发生的呢？

sentences.en: Well, Roman, it has to do with horses and staircases and a whole lot of hay.
sentences.zh: 嗯，罗曼，这跟马匹、楼梯以及一大堆干草有关。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I have no idea where this is going because I'm pretty sure horses can't use fire poles.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道这要扯到哪里去，因为我很确定马不会用消防滑杆。

sentences.en: But I can't wait to learn more.
sentences.zh: 但我等不及想了解更多了。

sentences.en: Roman, have you ever been inside a fire station?
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你进过消防局吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I've been to them.
sentences.zh: 去过，我去过一些。

sentences.en: Yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: There's lots of different ones.
sentences.zh: 有很多不同的消防局。

sentences.en: There's a cool round one in sort of the Albany-Berkeley junction that I've been inside.
sentences.zh: 在奥尔巴尼和伯克利交界处附近有一个很酷的圆形消防局，我进去过。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So the traditional structure of most firehouses of the 1800s, like Engine 21, were built three stories high.
sentences.zh: 所以19世纪大多数消防局的传统结构，比如第21消防连，都是建有三层楼高。

sentences.en: The horses were stabled on the first floor, the humans sleeping and eating quarters on the second, hay on the third, and a set of stairs connecting them.
sentences.zh: 马匹养在一楼，人类的起居和进食区在二楼，干草在三楼，楼梯将它们连接起来。

sentences.en: It worked pretty well, except that the horses would often follow the smell of human food and try to climb up the stairs.
sentences.zh: 这运作得挺好，除了马匹经常会顺着人类食物的气味试图爬上楼梯。

sentences.en: And horses can make it up a set of stairs just fine, but when it comes to going down the stairs, they'd often get stuck.
sentences.zh: 马匹上楼梯完全没问题，但如果要下楼梯，它们经常会卡住。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: That sounds harrowing.
sentences.zh: 听起来令人揪心。

sentences.en: Now, Roman, we've never had to remove a spooked horse from the stairway at work, have we?
sentences.zh: 现在，罗曼，我们在工作中可从没处理过从楼梯上受惊的马，对吧？

sentences.en: No, no, definitely not.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有，绝对没有。

sentences.en: Thank goodness.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地。

sentences.en: But if we did, we'd quickly find a way to make sure that doesn't happen again.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们遇到过，我们很快就会想出办法确保这种事不再发生。

sentences.en: That's something that happens once.
sentences.zh: 那是只会发生一次的事。

sentences.en: So to solve for this problem, most fire companies blocked off the old stairs, and they put in one very tight spiral staircase, which was fully horseproof.
sentences.zh: 为了解决这个问题，大多数消防连封堵了旧楼梯，并安装了一个非常狭窄的螺旋楼梯，这完全是防马的。

sentences.en: But this caused a new problem.
sentences.zh: 但这引发了一个新问题。

sentences.en: It took a lot longer for a team of firefighters to get down a tight spiral staircase.
sentences.zh: 消防员队伍通过狭窄的螺旋楼梯下楼要花很长时间。

sentences.en: And if Engine 21's firefighters were too slow out the door, they wouldn't be the first to the fire.
sentences.zh: 如果第21消防连的消防员出门太慢，他们就无法第一个赶到火灾现场。

sentences.en: And if it happened too often, they couldn't save lives, couldn't make a living, and their reputation might suffer, too,
sentences.zh: 如果这种情况经常发生，他们就无法拯救生命、无法谋生，他们的声誉也可能会受损，

sentences.en: to the point where maybe they'd stop getting calls altogether.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能再也接不到报警电话了。

sentences.en: Engine 21's total existence brought on competition.
sentences.zh: 第21消防连的整体生存状况伴随着竞争。

sentences.en: In order for Engine 21 to survive during that time period, they had to do everything right.
sentences.zh: 为了让第21消防连在那段时期生存下来，他们必须把每件事都做好。

sentences.en: They had to be correct.
sentences.zh: 他们必须无可挑剔。

sentences.en: Couldn't get into altercations on the street when people would call them out of their name.
sentences.zh: 当人们用难听的外号挑衅他们时，他们不能在街上跟人争吵。

sentences.en: And I've read many instances where they went into bars or taverns and were not served, even in uniform.
sentences.zh: 我读过很多次这样的例子：他们走进酒吧或小酒馆，哪怕穿着制服也遭到拒绝服务。

sentences.en: And that's kind of how it went for a couple years.
sentences.zh: 事情差不多就是这样过了几年。

sentences.en: And then one night in 1878, Engine 21 firefighter George Reed was in the hayloft on the third floor when the alarm went off.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1878年的一个晚上，第21消防连的消防员乔治·里德正在三楼的干草阁里，这时警报响了。

sentences.en: He acted on instinct, and instead of running down two flights of spiral stairs to catch up to the group,
sentences.zh: 他凭直觉行事，没有跑两层螺旋楼梯去追赶队伍，

sentences.en: he just slid down a pole from the third floor all the way down to the firSt.
sentences.zh: 而是直接从一根杆子从三楼滑到了一楼。

sentences.en: Wait, where did the pole come from?
sentences.zh: 等等，这根杆子是哪来的？

sentences.en: So the pole was a wooden binding pole that was used for securing hay to the wagon during transport.
sentences.zh: 这根杆子是一根木质捆绑杆，用于在运输过程中将干草固定在马车上。

sentences.en: When that pole wasn't in use, it was stored vertically from the loading area all the way up to the hayloft.
sentences.zh: 当这根杆子不用时，它就被垂直储存在从装货区一直到干草阁的地方。

sentences.en: So anyway, George was able to get saddled in and ready to go way before anyone else who took the winding staircase from the second floor.
sentences.zh: 总之，乔治系好装备准备出发的时间，要比任何走二楼旋转楼梯的人都要早得多。

sentences.en: And people were like, where did you come from?
sentences.zh: 大家都在问：你从哪儿冒出来的？

sentences.en: How'd you get here so fast?
sentences.zh: 你怎么来得这么快？

sentences.en: And then later, Engine 21's captain, Captain Kenyon, was like, let's install a permanent hole in the floor,
sentences.zh: 后来，第21消防连的长官肯扬长官就想：让我们在地板上安个固定的洞，

sentences.en: run a three-inch round wooden pole through the hole, and why don't we just slide that instead of taking the stairs?
sentences.zh: 穿过这个洞放一根三英寸粗的圆形木杆，我们为什么不直接滑这个而不是走楼梯呢？

sentences.en: So they did.
sentences.zh: 于是他们照做了。

sentences.en: So they get down three stories really, really faSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他们能非常非常快地穿过三层楼下到底楼。

sentences.en: Does it actually help them get to the fires first?
sentences.zh: 这真的能帮他们第一个到达火灾现场吗？

sentences.en: Well, I should say that DeKalb told me that at first, Engine 21 was the butt of many jokes because of the pole.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我得说，德卡尔夫告诉我，起初第21消防连因为这根杆子成了许多笑话的笑柄。

sentences.en: So they were laughed at, you know, it was a joke to everybody else, but it stopped being a joke when they found out that Engine 21 was putting out their fires getting in firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他们被嘲笑，你知道的，对其他人来说这就是个笑话，但当大家发现第21消防连总是最先赶到并扑灭火灾时，这就不再是笑话了。

sentences.en: And the city, as a matter of fact, annual report for April of 1878 stated that sliding poles increased members' response time.
sentences.zh: 事实上，芝加哥市1878年4月的年度报告指出，滑杆提高了队员的响应时间。

sentences.en: And as a result, sliding poles were being installed throughout Chicago, throughout all the firehouses in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 因此，滑杆开始在芝加哥全市安装，普及到芝加哥所有的消防局。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I mean, I can imagine that sliding down a pole, instead of going down a tight spiral staircase, would shave off a few seconds.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我可以想象，滑杆滑下去而不是走狭窄的螺旋楼梯，确实能省下好几秒钟。

sentences.en: But it doesn't sound like a lot of time, but maybe, you know, that's enough of an edge.
sentences.zh: 但这听起来好像时间不多，不过也许，你知道的，这就足够构成优势了。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe that's the difference between life and death in some situations.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在某些情况下，这可能是生与死的区别。

sentences.en: That could mean everything.
sentences.zh: 那可能意味着一切。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And Engine 21 didn't just install a pole.
sentences.zh: 而且第21消防连不只是安装了一根杆子。

sentences.en: They turned that pole into their skill, one that set them apart from all other fire companies.
sentences.zh: 他们把那根杆子练成了绝活，成了让他们在所有消防连中脱颖而出的标志。

sentences.en: Because it's not as easy as it looks to slide efficiently down a thin wooden pole, multiple flights of stairs.
sentences.zh: 因为要高效地顺着细细的木杆、穿过多层楼梯滑下来，可没看上去那么容易。

sentences.en: But they became very good at their craft.
sentences.zh: 但他们把这门手艺练得炉火纯青。

sentences.en: They would drill in the daytime.
sentences.zh: 他们在白天进行训练。

sentences.en: They had—their time frame was 12 to 14 seconds getting out of the door.
sentences.zh: 他们出门的时间限制是12到14秒。

sentences.en: That's astounding.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了。

sentences.en: We can't do that today.
sentences.zh: 我们现在做不到。

sentences.en: They would drill regularly doing that, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，他们会对此进行常规训练。

sentences.en: They would slide the pole, hook the horses up and out the door.
sentences.zh: 他们会滑下铁杆，给马套上鞍具，然后冲出大门。

sentences.en: They went.
sentences.zh: 他们出发了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: In 12 to 14 seconds.
sentences.zh: 就在12到14秒内。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The fire pole, it revolutionized the way firefighters responded to emergencies.
sentences.zh: 消防滑杆彻底改变了消防员应对紧急情况的方式。

sentences.en: And eventually they were installed around the world.
sentences.zh: 最终，它们被安装到了世界各地。

sentences.en: Like you said, it saved lives.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，它挽救了生命。

sentences.en: But the pole also created a new kind of problem for firefighters, a new kind of life-or-death problem.
sentences.zh: 但滑杆也给消防员带来了另一种问题，一种生死攸关的新问题。

sentences.en: Because in leaping onto the pole and accelerating, firefighters were sometimes injuring themselves before they even got to the scene.
sentences.zh: 因为消防员在跃上滑杆并加速时，有时甚至还没到达现场就受伤了。

sentences.en: I've heard stories of intoxicated firemen going to reach the slide, the pole, miss the pole.
sentences.zh: 我听说过有些喝醉的消防员去抓滑杆时，结果抓空了。

sentences.en: And his head was the first thing that hit the concrete.
sentences.zh: 然后他的头部是第一个撞到水泥地上的。

sentences.en: Sprained ankles, concussions, falls.
sentences.zh: 脚踝扭伤、脑震荡、跌落。

sentences.en: Some inebriated or sleepwalking firefighters have simply wandered over the hole and fallen into it, accidentally falling 20 or 30 feet.
sentences.zh: 有些喝醉酒或梦游的消防员不小心走过洞口掉了进去，意外坠落了20或30英尺。

sentences.en: And at their most dangerous, the poles have led to deaths.
sentences.zh: 而在最危险的情况下，这些滑杆甚至导致了人员死亡。

sentences.en: Today, fire poles have been phased out of use in a lot of cities.
sentences.zh: 如今，许多城市的消防滑杆已经逐渐被淘汰。

sentences.en: So if firefighters aren't using fire poles, are they back to using spiral staircases?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果消防员不用消防滑杆了，他们是改回螺旋楼梯了吗？

sentences.en: Well, without horses, there's no need for horse-proof staircases.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没有了马，自然就不需要防马的楼梯了。

sentences.en: If that makes sense, yeah, okay.
sentences.zh: 如果这说得通的话，对，好吧。

sentences.en: In multi-story firehouses, some have considered installing slides and other straight staircases,
sentences.zh: 在多层消防局里，有些人考虑过安装滑梯和其他直楼梯，

sentences.en: although both options are slower than what Engine 21's response time was with the pole.
sentences.zh: 尽管这两种选择都比21号消防车当年用滑杆时的出警速度要慢。

sentences.en: And most newer fire stations now operate from a single story, if space permits, so they're on the ground floor already.
sentences.zh: 而且现在大多数较新的消防站如果空间允许，都是单层运作的，所以他们已经在底楼了。

sentences.en: But all this doesn't mean that you won't see a fire pole in your local firehouse anymore.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着你在当地的消防局里再也看不到消防滑杆了。

sentences.en: Just that, over time, it's really just become a symbol.
sentences.zh: 只是随着时间的推移，它真的变成了一个象征。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, considering that it went through a phase of non-existing, it existed for a while, and now it's being phased out,
sentences.zh: 对啊，我的意思是，考虑到它经历过不被使用的阶段，存在了一段时间，而现在又在逐渐淘汰，

sentences.en: it really has stuck in the popular imagination.
sentences.zh: 它确实深深扎根于大众的想象中。

sentences.en: Like, if you'd ask anyone what they'd find in a firehouse, they would, you know, talk about an engine, maybe a Dalmatian,
sentences.zh: 比如说，如果你问任何人消防局里有什么，他们肯定会谈到消防车，可能还有一只斑点狗，

sentences.en: and then there would be, like, a pole.
sentences.zh: 然后就会有一根滑杆之类的东西。

sentences.en: Like, my kids could tell you about a fire pole, even though they probably weren't in active use during their lifetimes.
sentences.zh: 就像我的孩子们会跟你讲消防滑杆一样，尽管在他们有生之年，这些滑杆可能已经不常投入使用了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I even read an article with an architect who specializes in firehouse design,
sentences.zh: 我甚至读过一篇采访某位专门从事消防局设计建筑师的文章，

sentences.en: and he said that in his latest designs, fire poles were specifically requested by city administrators
sentences.zh: 他说在他最新的设计中，城市管理者专门要求安装消防滑杆，

sentences.en: because of what they represented, even though the firefighters these days wouldn't necessarily use them.
sentences.zh: 因为它们所代表的意义，尽管现在的消防员不一定会去使用它们。

sentences.en: These days, it's just simultaneously an emblem of innovation and of tradition.
sentences.zh: 如今，它同时成为了创新与传统的象征。

sentences.en: Well, it's so cool.
sentences.zh: 这太酷了。

sentences.en: I'm so glad I know more about fire poles.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能对消防滑杆有更多了解。

sentences.en: This is great, Lasha.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了，拉莎。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。
